GO:0085041 arbuscule is an is_a child of GO:0085035, whereas literature often distinguishes arbuscules from parasitic haustoria. Preserve that attributed umbrella usage: the definition is not restricted to pathogenicity, but arbuscule formation is not asserted as an exact synonym or given a new hierarchy here. The GO membrane-invagination definition does not describe every tremelloid micropore interface. No xrefs or SSSOM equivalences are asserted. Parasitic-plant haustorial organs are outside this microbial hyphal scope; fungi and oomycetes are both included. Fungal arbuscule formation now has its own source-bounded phenotype record, traitmech:000664. This resolves the missing record reference, not the umbrella hierarchy question; no subclass or disjointness relationship between these two phenotypes is asserted.

gap-ba3eb32b17e56b53bd425674f0a5751978a9.prompt: Retain sequential nutrient use without imposing a universal lag or regulatory mechanism.
gap-ba3eb32b17e56b53bd425674f0a5751978a9.rationale: Boulineau's Introduction defines sequential carbon use, while lag-emphasizing accounts operationalize a narrower growth-curve pattern. Wang reports short or nonexistent lags; Sandercock and Page extend the observed scope to nitrogen-source transitions. The present definition uses the nutrient-switching sense and does not require glucose preference, a positive minimum lag, complete arrest of every cell or strictly zero secondary-substrate use. An arbitrary biphasic growth curve without nutrient-switching evidence is insufficient. Diauxic shift denotes the transition; polyauxie and unqualified diphasic growth are not exact synonyms. METPO:1000731 nutrient adaptation is a trophic-type class whose local record operationalizes chronic copiotroph/oligotroph nutrient regimes, not this temporal pattern. Phenotype is the conservative parent pending upstream hierarchy review. Generalist and specialist denote niche breadth; dormancy, carbon catabolite repression and generic resource-use predicates are not exact equivalents.

Resolve context-dependent same-sex mating terminology and external phenotype/process mappings before adding synonyms or xrefs. The existing homothallism evidence note, citing DOI:10.5598/imafungus.2015.06.01.13, groups unisexual reproduction within a homothallism umbrella. That wording conflicts with interpreting the current single-isolate self-fertility definition as a universal superclass here. Our scope decision interprets the umbrella as including unisexual selfing, not as evidence that every same-type outcrossing partner is independently self-fertile. Preserve the older source attribution and retain phenotype while the operational and umbrella scopes await curator reconciliation; issue #1703 records this explicit distinction.

gap-cf7a17405f6336d89bcd1fd3c914442eee23.rationale: Killing susceptible nematodes is required; reversible paralysis, repellence, reduced egg hatch, host defense induction and a sequence annotation alone are insufficient. Predatory bacterium (traitmech:000054) requires consuming bacterial prey. Animal pathogen METPO:1004002 requires infection, unnecessary for culture-derived toxicity. Phenotype METPO:1000059 is the conservative parent. Pinned/current METPO inspection found no exact active or deprecated counterpart. CHEBI:25491 denotes a nematicide chemical, not this microbial capability, and is not an xref. No exact synonyms or organism-level disjointness are asserted; v596 proposes the class. The methodological context below cautions against equating immobility or a negative NaOH response with death under all conditions. It is not evidence of microbial killing or definition support.

gap-d312732f210d079c032068ee2b54b4931eca.prompt: BSL-2 requires a biosafety cabinet specifically for procedures with aerosol or splash potential, while other work may go on the open bench. Which procedures actually generate an infectious dose at the breathing zone, and does the current procedure list match them?

proposed_experiments.approach: non-infectious tracer release with breathing-zone sampling
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: whether any open-bench procedure exceeds the breathing-zone tracer recovery of cabinet-required procedures
model_systems: bacteriophage or fluorescent-bead surrogate at defined titre
a working BSL-2 laboratory
breathing-zone and area impingers
proposed_experiments.name: Surrogate-tracer aerosol survey of routine BSL-2 procedures
perturbations: each routine procedure performed on the open bench
the same procedure performed inside a class II cabinet
deliberate worst-case variants such as a dropped tube
readouts: tracer recovered at the breathing zone per procedure
particle size distribution in the respirable fraction
surface deposition beyond the immediate work area
proposed_experiments.would_refute: an off-list procedure matches or exceeds a listed one -- the control boundary is misplaced
proposed_experiments.would_support: recovery tracks the existing list -- the procedure boundary is drawn where the aerosol actually is

gap-d312732f210d079c032068ee2b54b4931eca.rationale: The bench/cabinet boundary is the single control that most BSL-2 work turns on, and it is drawn from procedure lists that long predate quantitative aerosol measurement. A procedure that is on the open bench but does generate respirable particles is an unrecognised exposure; one needlessly in the cabinet costs throughput. Either way the edge into biosafety_cabinet is asserting something measurable that has not been measured.

gap-de2e32a02ba14ffa8f74d45a8822f0b33234.prompt: This record commits to luminal oxygen limitation contributing to the primary fermenter community. Does the reverse arm hold too -- do the fermenters and the epithelium maintain the anoxia -- making this a feedback loop rather than the one-way edge drawn?

proposed_experiments.approach: staged gnotobiotic colonisation with in situ oxygen microsensing
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: whether luminal oxygen rises when an established fermenter community is depleted, with colonisation order held constant
model_systems: germ-free animals colonised in defined stages
a defined community with and without obligate anaerobe fermenters
oxygen microelectrodes at the mucosal surface and mid-lumen
proposed_experiments.name: Oxygen microprofiling during staged gnotobiotic colonisation
perturbations: colonisation with facultative organisms alone
subsequent addition of obligate anaerobe fermenters
butyrate supplementation without the producing community
antibiotic depletion of an established fermenter community
readouts: luminal and mucosal oxygen partial pressure over time
community composition by shotgun sequencing
short-chain fatty acid concentration
epithelial hypoxia by pimonidazole staining
proposed_experiments.would_refute: oxygen is unchanged by depletion -- the habitat sets the anoxia and the single existing edge is the whole story
proposed_experiments.would_support: oxygen rises on depletion and falls again on re-colonisation -- the return arm is real and the pair is a loop

gap-de2e32a02ba14ffa8f74d45a8822f0b33234.rationale: The existing edge is not wrong so much as half: it says the anoxic lumen permits the fermenters, and stops. If the return arm also holds, the two nodes are a self-reinforcing loop, and losing the fermenters raises luminal oxygen and admits facultative pathogens -- the collapse that follows antibiotic depletion. That is the clinically load-bearing half, and a graph of one-way edges can only carry it if someone draws it.
gap-de2e32a02ba14ffa8f74d45a8822f0b33234.resolution_note: Supported, with two bounds. The would_support criterion was 'oxygen rises on depletion and falls again on re-colonisation', and both arms hold: streptomycin depletion of butyrate-producing Clostridia lowers cecal butyrate and raises epithelial oxygenation, tributyrin supplementation reverses it, and recolonisation with 17 human Clostridia isolates raises butyrate and restores colonocyte hypoxia (DOI:10.1016/j.chom.2016.03.004), replicated independently by DOI:10.1016/j.chom.2015.03.005. The pair is therefore a feedback loop, now modelled as such. Bound 1: the return arm is HOST-MEDIATED, running through butyrate and colonocyte beta-oxidation rather than direct microbial oxygen consumption (DOI:10.1126/science.aam9949), so the graph routes it through the new butyrate and colonocyte_oxidative_metabolism nodes rather than drawing a direct reverse edge. Bound 2: the community is NOT responsible for bulk centre-lumen anoxia -- direct phosphorescent-probe measurement finds germ-free and conventional mice nearly indistinguishable (DOI:10.1073/pnas.1718635115) -- so the closing edge is scoped to mucosal-to-luminal oxygen flux and carries that source as bounding evidence. Left open and tracked in issue 617: whether abiotic luminal oxygen consumption deserves its own node, and whether this component should attach to the trait node, which no current source supports.
